content.user_title: Manage Azure File Shares with TypeScript
content.value_statement: Azure File Share SDK work can be hard to map from concept to code. This skill gives focused TypeScript examples for authentication, shares, directories, files, metadata, SAS, and errors.
actual_capabilities: Shows authentication patterns for connection strings, shared keys, DefaultAzureCredential, and SAS tokens.
Demonstrates creating, listing, deleting, and configuring Azure file shares.
Covers directory creation, listing, existence checks, and deletion workflows.
Explains file upload and download options using strings, buffers, streams, and local file paths.
Includes metadata, HTTP header, range, snapshot, SAS, and RestError handling examples.
Summarizes Node.js and browser support differences for key SDK features.
limitations: It is a reference skill and does not connect to Azure or validate credentials for the user.
Examples assume @azure/storage-file-share 12.x and Node.js 18 or newer.
It does not provision Azure Storage accounts, roles, networks, or file share permissions.
Browser support is limited for shared keys, local file paths, streams, buffers, and SAS generation.

use_cases.title: Build File Share Workflows
use_cases.description: Create backend upload, download, and metadata flows using the Azure Files SDK.

use_cases.title: Standardize Storage Examples
use_cases.description: Use consistent TypeScript examples for shares, directories, files, snapshots, and SAS tokens.

use_cases.title: Debug Azure Files Integration
use_cases.description: Map common SDK errors, authentication options, and platform limits during implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Authentication
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new Azure Files project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose an authentication method for @azure/storage-file-share. My app runs in [environment], and I need [development or production] guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Create Share Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Show a TypeScript workflow for creating an Azure file share, creating a nested directory, and checking whether the directory exists.

prompt_templates.title: Design File Transfer
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan an Azure File Share upload and download flow for [file size] files in Node.js. Include the best SDK methods and error handling points.

prompt_templates.title: Review Advanced Storage Pattern
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Azure Files design for snapshots, SAS permissions, metadata, and range operations. Identify security and reliability improvements.

output_examples.input: I need to upload a large local file to Azure Files from Node.js.
output: Recommended approach: use a stream-based upload for large files.
Check the local file size before creating the remote file.
Use bounded concurrency and handle RestError status codes for retries or user messages.

output_examples.input: I need temporary read access to one file in a share.
output: Recommended approach: generate a file-level SAS with read-only permissions.
Use a short expiration time and avoid broad share permissions.
Return the URL only to the caller that requested access.

output_examples.input: I need to support both browser and Node.js clients.
output: Use browser-compatible authentication such as SAS or anonymous access where appropriate.
Keep shared key credential and local file APIs on the server side.
Document separate transfer paths for browser uploads and Node.js file operations.

best_practices: Prefer managed identity or DefaultAzureCredential for production services when possible.
Use short-lived, least-privilege SAS tokens for delegated access.
Choose stream and range operations for large files or partial updates.
anti_patterns: Do not embed account keys, connection strings, or SAS tokens in source code.
Do not use broad share SAS permissions when one file or one operation is enough.
Do not assume Node.js-only APIs work in browser-based applications.

faq.question: What package does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers @azure/storage-file-share for TypeScript and JavaScript applications.

faq.question: Does it support Azure Blob Storage?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on Azure Files SMB file shares, not Blob Storage containers.

faq.question: Can it generate production-ready code?
faq.answer: It provides implementation patterns, but you should adapt security, retries, logging, and deployment settings.

faq.question: Which authentication method should I use?
faq.answer: Use DefaultAzureCredential for production when available. Use connection strings or shared keys only when appropriate.

faq.question: Can browser apps use all examples?
faq.answer: No. Shared keys, local file paths, streams, buffers, SAS generation, and DefaultAzureCredential are Node.js-only here.

faq.question: Does the skill execute Azure operations itself?
faq.answer: No. It is documentation with examples that users can adapt in their own projects.
